topic: Google's new AI "coworker" agents get their own work email, calendar and Drive
post:
Your next coworker might have an email address… and no pulse. 📧🤖
Google just gave AI agents their own work accounts.

Google Cloud announced Gemini Agent, with "coworker" agents that can get their own Workspace identity.

Here's the breakdown 👇

📬 Each coworker agent can get its own @agents.company.com email, a calendar, Drive storage, and a spot in the company directory
💬 Colleagues can @mention it in Chat or tag it in a Doc comment
✏️ Its edits show up under its own name in version history
🔐 Its actions go to an audit trail tied to the agent, not a person, and it only sees files explicitly shared with it

The catch: it's in private preview. Google hasn't shared pricing, plans or a general release date.

Why it matters:
Last week we talked about agents acting with no clear ID. This is the opposite approach: give agents a name tag, a paper trail and limited access, like any new hire.
The question shifts from "can AI do the work?" to "how do we manage AI teammates?"

Practical takeaway:
If your company adopts agents, ask 3 questions first: Who owns this agent? What can it access? Where's the log of what it did?

Would you be comfortable working alongside an AI teammate with its own inbox? 👇
